reason: The text explicitly describes the congregation (כָּל־ עֲדַ֤ת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל - 'all the congregation of the children of Israel') murmuring against Moses and Aaron in the aftermath of Korah's rebellion (verse 41). The people complain against their leaders, saying 'You have killed the people of the LORD' (אַתֶּ֥ם הֲמִתֶּ֖ם אֶת־ עַ֥ם יְהוָֽה), demonstrating clear antagonism. This murmuring represents opposition and hostility from the general population toward their appointed leaders.
